claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys is governed by a balance between configurational entropy and lattice-distortion energy.
Al is the primary source of atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion in this alloy system.
Within an optimal Al-concentration window, lattice distortion stabilizes a disordered single-phase, potentially fcc, solid solution.
A disordered single-phase structure facilitates sluggish diffusion and defect management.
Sluggish diffusion and defect management enable high-temperature strength, radiation tolerance, environmental resistance, and cryogenic toughness.
Excessive or inadequately tuned lattice distortion causes local chemical ordering or precipitation.
Local ordering or precipitation undermines the desired combination of properties.
Low-to-moderate-Al Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys can be processed as single-phase disordered, commonly fcc, solid solutions.
Such low-to-moderate-Al single-phase alloys are known to have excellent mechanical and corrosion properties.
Homogenization and annealing cause the samples to reach equilibrium.
Changing Al content while holding the other elemental ratios constant changes local lattice distortion and short-range chemical ordering.
Moderate Al additions increase lattice-distortion energy.
Increased lattice-distortion energy makes configurational entropy more effective at stabilizing a disordered single-phase structure.
The Al-induced distorted lattice slows atomic diffusion.
The distorted lattice resists environmental degradation and radiation-induced defect agglomeration.
The distorted fcc lattice supports cryogenic deformation mechanisms such as nanotwinning, thereby improving toughness.
Exceeding an optimal distortion threshold promotes ordering or precipitate formation and degrades strength, ductility, and environmental performance.
Alloys in the optimal Al range will retain a single disordered phase and outperform low- and high-Al alloys in high-temperature strength, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Outside the critical Al/distortion window, secondary phases or ordered regions will form and the balanced properties will be lost.
